content: Regular foot evaluations are critical for identifying risk factors that may lead to the development of ulcers or necessitate amputations. Foot examinations should comprehensively include assessments of the skin, sensory function, pulse checks, and neurological evaluations. Patients who exhibit sensory loss or have existing foot ulcers should undergo foot evaluations during every clinical visit. Individuals with a history of foot complications must be provided with appropriate and protective footwear to prevent further issues. Vascular screening is strongly recommended for patients presenting with foot symptoms or those who have risk factors for peripheral arterial disease (PAD). Specialized foot care, which may include custom footwear and advanced therapeutic interventions, should be made available to individuals who are at high risk for foot-related complications.
